claim: County board of equalization and review is composed of the county commissioners unless a special board is appointed.
The board holds its first meeting not earlier than the first Monday in April and not later than the first Monday in May.
In a revaluation year the board must finish by December 1.
A taxpayer's hearing request must be made in writing or by personal appearance before the board adjourns.
The board must notify the appellant by mail of its action within 30 days after adjournment.
Counties must reappraise all real property at least every eighth year; counties of 75,000+ must advance reappraisal if sales assessment ratio is below .85 or above 1.15.
UNCONFIRMED: Deadline to appeal a county board decision to the NC Property Tax Commission (commonly stated as 30 days) was not opened on an official page.
UNCONFIRMED: Specific county revaluation years not verified.
Elderly or disabled exclusion: greater of $25,000 or 50% of appraised value of a permanent residence is excluded.
Qualifying owner must be 65+ or totally and permanently disabled, an NC resident, with prior-year income not over the income eligibility limit, as of January 1.
Income limit started at $25,000 for 2008 and is adjusted yearly by the Social Security COLA; NCDOR sets it each year.
Application should be filed in the regular listing period but must be accepted through June 1 preceding the tax year.
Circuit breaker: owner 65+/disabled with 5 years' ownership and occupancy and income up to 150% of the limit may defer taxes above 4% (or 5%) of income.
Circuit breaker deferred taxes (prior 3 years) become due when the owner transfers the residence, dies (unless passing to co-owner/spouse who occupies), or stops using it as permanent residence.
Circuit breaker application also accepted through June 1.
UNCONFIRMED: Current-year dollar income eligibility limit not confirmed (NCDOR AV-9 2026 is a PDF, not opened).
Excise tax is $1.00 on each $500 (or fraction) of consideration or value of the interest conveyed.
The transferor (seller) must pay the tax to the register of deeds before recording.
For land in multiple counties, tax is paid in the county containing the greater part by value.
Half of proceeds go to the county general fund; half goes to the State (less county allowance).
Exempt transfers include by operation of law, lease, will, intestacy, gift, no consideration, merger, and instruments securing debt.
Power-of-sale foreclosure may not proceed unless authorized by a court after a hearing before the clerk of superior court.
Notice of hearing must be served not less than 10 days before the hearing; posting service not less than 20 days before.
Clerk must find valid debt, default, right to foreclose, notice, and no bar (home-loan pre-foreclosure notice; military protection).
Clerk's findings may be appealed to district or superior court within 10 days.
Notice of sale must be posted at least 20 days before sale and published once a week for two successive weeks; mailed first-class at least 20 days before.
Lenders in many cases must send a pre-foreclosure notice at least 45 days before filing.
Judicial foreclosure (civil action) is filed in district or superior court and heard by a judge.
After a foreclosure sale there is a 10-day period for upset bids; each upset bid restarts a 10-day period.
Upset bid must exceed the prior bid by 5% with minimum increase of $750, with deposit of at least 5% (not less than $750) filed with clerk.
Sale becomes final when no upset bid is filed within the 10-day period.
Trustee records a trustee's deed and files an accounting with the clerk; occupants may be removed through court.
Tax-foreclosure sale is by public auction at the courthouse door.
UNCONFIRMED: Role of sheriff vs. trustee/commissioner in conducting sales by county not verified.
The elected Clerk of Superior Court acts as probate judge.
Letters testamentary or of administration are issued by the clerk; filing fee quoted as $120.
Land and houses generally are not administered through the probate estate unless the will provides or sale is needed to pay debts.
Collection by affidavit: intestate estate personal property up to $20,000 (up to $30,000 for surviving spouse sole heir), after 30 days.
Summary administration is available when the surviving spouse is sole heir or devisee.
Transfers by a fiduciary administering an estate are exempt from the residential property disclosure statement.
UNCONFIRMED: Affidavit procedure under 28A-25-1 covers personal property; its use to sell real property not confirmed.
G.S. 105-32.2 (estate tax) repealed effective January 1, 2013, applicable to decedents dying on or after that date.
NCDOR table notes SL 2013-316 s.7(a) repeals NC estate tax for decedents dying on or after Jan 1, 2013.

Register of deeds recording fee: $26 for first 15 pages plus $4 per additional page for general instruments.
Deed of trust or mortgage: $64 for first 35 pages plus $4 per additional page.
No fee for recording satisfaction or cancellation of a deed of trust or mortgage.
$25 extra fee for documents not meeting recording standards.
Fees are collected before filing; fees listed are exclusive.
Excise tax must be paid to register of deeds before recording the deed.

Preparing deeds is the practice of law; unlicensed persons or website providers may not prepare deeds conveying NC real property.
Transfers with no consideration or by gift are exempt from excise tax.

Property tax lien attaches on the date property is to be listed (January 1, per 105-285 cross-reference).
Penalties, interest and costs attach at the same time as the tax lien.
Tax lien foreclosure by civil action in the nature of a mortgage foreclosure; owner of record, spouse and lienholders must be served.
Court-ordered sale is free of liens except certain items (undetermined taxes, non-party taxes, C-PACE, conservation agreements).
In rem tax foreclosure under 105-375 has no hearing before judgment; an interested person may move to set aside before execution.

Commissioner may require a deposit up to 20% of the bid.
Exceptions or increased bids may be filed within 10 days after the report of sale.
Surplus proceeds go to those entitled; clerk holds if claims disputed.
Taxing units may bid at the sale and resell the property.
Summary ejectment applies to a tenant holding over after term expires or after lease breach by which estate ceased.
Clerk issues summons requiring answer at a time not exceeding seven days from issuance (excluding weekends and holidays).
Magistrate gives judgment for possession if plaintiff proves case, defendant admits, or defendant fails to appear.
Unpaid water, sewer or electric charges cannot be the basis for lease termination.

Foreclosure notice of sale on residential property under 15 units must be mailed to occupants under a rental agreement (or 'occupant').
NC courts refer to G.S. 45-21.33A for effect of foreclosure on a preexisting tenancy.
Tenants in possession under unrecorded leases are not 'record owners' for foreclosure notice.

Seller (transferor) pays NC excise tax of $1 per $500.
Preparing deeds and passing on title is the practice of law, requiring an NC licensed attorney.
Recording of satisfaction of deed of trust carries no register of deeds fee.

Contract for deed must be signed and acknowledged by all parties and a copy delivered at signing.
Purchaser may cancel until midnight of the third business day after execution or delivery.
Seller must record the contract or a memorandum within five business days of signing.
Contract must include a completed residential property disclosure unless seller selects 'No Representation'.
Purchaser's right to prepay without penalty must be included (exceptions if encumbered by deed of trust).
Forfeiture requires recorded mutual termination or court order; pre-default waivers of redemption are ineffective.
Owner must furnish purchaser a residential property disclosure statement on the Real Estate Commission standard form.
Owner may disclose known conditions or state 'no representations'.
Owner must also furnish an owners' association and mandatory covenants disclosure statement.
If owner selects 'no representations', no duty to disclose conditions, whether or not owner should have known.
Exempt transfers include court-ordered, foreclosure, fiduciary, co-owner, lineal/spouse, and divorce transfers.
First sale of never-inhabited dwelling and lease-option transfers are exempt from 47E-4 but not 47E-4.1.

Court divides marital and divisible property equitably; equal division is presumed.
Property acquired during marriage before separation is presumed marital; tenancy by entirety real property presumed marital.
Court may award a distributive award instead of in-kind distribution.
Party may record a lis pendens claiming real property is marital.
Transfers between spouses under a divorce decree or Chapter 50 distribution are exempt from disclosure statement.
Unlicensed persons may not prepare deeds or pass on title; attorney needed.
Seller must give purchaser the residential property disclosure statement.
Seller pays excise tax to register of deeds before recording.
Owner can state 'no representations' on disclosure statement, relieving duty to disclose unknown conditions.
Transfers by foreclosure sale are exempt from the disclosure statement.
Borrower may negotiate a loan modification or other resolution until the foreclosure sale is final.
